leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 files prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as the single prize part. They share the case: Katori's magic-wavelength idea, 1e-18 performance reproduced independently (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE), and the cleanest two-name credit. They also share the main reservations: overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, partial or unsettled credit for Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and others, and the pending redefinition of the second. They differ on how to word the citation (Johansson and Olsson want the lattice scheme and invention named; Kroll and Lindroth want many-body and interaction physics considered; Pearce and Lindroth want no reliance on the redefinition). Johansson, Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce each flag closeness to the field or to another candidate in their notes. Several of the five treat it as the cleanest candidate on attribution and maturity rather than as the most novel physics, and Danielsson and Eriksson, who prefer B003, do not oppose it.

Two of eight prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as the single part. They share the argument that a specific 2011 prediction was followed by the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, reproduced by many groups, and that it is a new physical regime and not a refinement. They share the reservations that the superconducting mechanism is debated and that Cao and other early experimental groups fall outside the three-name limit. Both say they would accept B024 first (Danielsson would be content to see it first; Eriksson would not oppose it as a strong second choice). Their citations are close but not identical: Danielsson names a magic twist angle, Eriksson says twisted bilayer graphene more generally.

One member prefers the statistical physics of active matter (Vicsek, Toner, Ramaswamy). The case is a minimal model with universal hydrodynamic and renormalization-group consequences and an understood mechanism. Mehlig himself states the reservations: only partial quantitative tests of the Toner-Tu exponents, a loosely bounded field, and the omission of Yuhai Tu. No other member lists B006 as a preference or alternative; Johansson and Lindroth ask which experiments test the exponents. Mehlig lists B003 and B023 as alternatives, not B024, though he says he would not seriously oppose colleagues on B024.

areas_of_agreement: Every file that prefers B024 or discusses it names the same two laureates, Katori and Ye, and no file proposes a different or larger set for that ballot.

B024 is described by supporters and non-supporters alike (including Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig) as mature and independently reproduced, with the cleanest attribution on the shortlist. The disagreement is over its kind and novelty, not its quality.

B003 appears as a preferred or alternative choice in the files of Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson, and the members who discuss it agree that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled and that Cao and other early experimentalists fall outside the three-name credit.
Members across the camps agree that the citation should rest on what has been demonstrated, not on a promised outcome such as the redefinition of the second.

B023 (topological insulators) is judged by Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig to have a difficult allocation because of Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes and the 3D contributors, plus overlap with the 2016 prize, and none of them prefers it as a lead.
B043 (circuit QED) is not pursued by anyone except its proposer, and Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce each raise overlap with the 2025 circuit prize and the omission of Wallraff.
scientific_disputes: Whether a precision-measurement advance (B024) counts as a new discovery or as a refinement of a lineage already recognised in 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (ion control). Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce say the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea; Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig give weight to the overlap.

Whether a new regime or phase of matter (B003) should outrank a quantitative leap in an existing capability. Danielsson and Eriksson say yes in principle; Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce point to unsettled pairing physics and twist-angle disorder.
Whether the Toner-Tu exponents and the active-matter framework (B006) have enough quantitative experimental confirmation for a prize, as Johansson and Lindroth ask.

Whether aberration-corrected electron optics (B001) is a discovery in physics or an enabling instrument whose impact comes through other fields; Olsson, who first proposed it, has moved it to an alternative.
Whether many-body and interaction physics inside the clock should be part of the B024 case (Kroll and Lindroth raise it) or the case should stay on the invention and its realisation.
attribution_disputes: B024: whether Lemonde (SYRTE), Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Ovsiannikov or the ion-clock groups hold claims that a two-name credit would pass over. Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson think the invention and the record accuracy sit with Katori and Ye; Johansson, Olsson and Pearce ask that the first demonstrations be checked.
B024: how to separate Katori's concept from Ye's record-accuracy work, and whether the latter counts as invention or as engineering and systematics control (Kroll, Mehlig).

B003: Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce would keep Bistritzer as first author of the prediction. Mehlig suggested a two-name configuration of MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and Lindroth notes omitting him is a real cost. Yuan Cao, Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov are outside any three-name credit.
B006: Yuhai Tu is outside the credited trio although the Toner-Tu theory was joint work (Mehlig, Lindroth).
B001: whether Krivanek's STEM corrector can be credited alongside Rose, Haider and Urban within three names (Olsson, Mehlig, Johansson, Danielsson, Pearce).

B014: four credited names (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Esslinger) against a three-person limit, with different proposed trios in the opening and a split between theory and experiment (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson).
B035: AMANDA, DUMAND and IceCube lineage and a large collaboration make three or two names contested (Danielsson, Pearce, Olsson); Pearce's own configuration lists Halzen and Karle only.
maturity_disputes: B003: Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each mention the unsettled superconducting mechanism. Danielsson and Eriksson argue that the Nobel Prize has not required a settled mechanism and cite robust reproduction; Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson want a few more years of consolidation.

B024: the SI second has not been redefined. Kroll and Lindroth say this should not be a condition and that the clocks already meet the criteria; Eriksson asked whether it is necessary for timing; Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce note the payoff is still pending.
B006: only partial experimental tests of the exponents, and a loosely bounded field (Mehlig himself; Johansson and Lindroth press the point).
B035: the diffuse flux is well established but source identification is still partial (Danielsson, Pearce), so the discovery is mature while the interpretation is young.
B043: a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025 raises a balance question rather than a maturity question (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B043 proposer) directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, knows the credited B043 names professionally, and says he should recuse or discount his B043 ranking; he notes no specific conflict for B024, B023 or B014. He now prefers B024.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Hall is a former collaborator of Jun Ye (B024); Kroll says there is no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye and asks the committee to weigh the lineage connection when considering recusal.

Olsson is an electron microscopist who works with aberration-corrected instruments (B001) and has flagged proximity to the field as a possible reason for recusal on B001; she has moved B001 to an alternative.
Lindroth works in theoretical atomic physics adjacent to B024 and B014, and says that is a possible bias and not a recusal issue; she has no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye.

Pearce (chair) is close in subject to the IceCube (B035) and Higgs (B010) communities and collaborates in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, but not with the credited names; he would flag proximity if B035 were seriously considered. He notes no conflict on B024.

Mehlig notes a co-written 2020 review on machine learning for active matter (no collaboration with the B006 names) and that Olsson and Johansson are in the same Gothenburg physics environment; Danielsson and Eriksson report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B024, does the committee accept Katori and Ye as the complete credit, and what do Lindroth, Kroll, Johansson and Olsson, as the atomic and optical physics voices, say about the specific claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Hinkley for the first demonstrations and for the 1e-18 milestones?

Can the B024 case be written as a discovery distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and how would the citation word it (lattice scheme and invention, accuracy, many-body physics) without relying on the pending redefinition of the second?

For B003, is an unresolved superconducting mechanism a bar to a prize in 2026 or an ordinary open question, and what would the members who prefer it need to see to support waiting a year or two instead?

For B003, is a three-name credit of MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer defensible given Cao and other early experiments, and would Danielsson and Eriksson accept a citation that names the discovery without implying complete experimental credit? Is dropping Bistritzer, as Mehlig suggested, acceptable to anyone else?
Mehlig (B006) has no other explicit supporter. Which published experiments quantitatively test the Toner-Tu exponents, and does Tu's omission weaken a three-name credit?

Is there a different single-part or multi-part configuration that members would join, for example the compatibility of B003 with B024 as a two-part prize, given that Danielsson noted the combined number of names would exceed three under the supplied credits? Which members would explicitly support that, and would any file's alternatives change?

For B035 and B001, what concretely would resolve the credit questions (AMANDA and DUMAND lineage, Krivanek's STEM corrector), and does any member wish to move either from alternative to preferred configuration?
summary.chair_observation: In round 1 five of eight files prefer B024, two prefer B003, and one prefers B006. No file prefers a multi-part configuration. The B024 camp gives the cleanest attribution and maturity as its grounds and acknowledges the novelty and credit questions. The B003 camp grants B024 maturity and attribution and values a new regime of matter, while members outside it name the unsettled mechanism and the Cao omission. Round 2 should settle the B024 credit boundary and citation wording, the B003 maturity and attribution questions, and Mehlig's request for experimental evidence on B006, not re-argue positions already stated.
